prs.title: fix(formatter_markdown): honor range ignore inside directives
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Fixes #28154

Range ignore is supported only at the top level.

Prettier does not support directives, so the contents of `:::` end up at the top level and the range works there.
We parse `:::` as a container directive, so its contents were not top-level and the range was ignored.

This PR treats a `:::` directive with no blockquote / list item / footnote above it as top-level.

Supporting ranges everywhere is possible, but it has concerns such as indentation drift in verbatim output. So this starts small.

prs.title: fix(formatter): keep closing HTML comments at the start of a line
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
The three new Annex B declaration fixtures in #28057 parse successfully but fail after formatting. A comment between `let` and its binding moves onto the keyword's line: `let --> comment`. A closing HTML comment is recognized only at the start of a line, so this changes the program or produces invalid syntax.

Force a hard line break before closing HTML comments. Add a formatter snapshot covering `let`, `const`, and destructuring declarations, and document the divergence from Prettier 3.9.10, whose output is rejected by `node --check`.

Based on the merged submodule update. `just submodules`, `just coverage`, full `just test -p oxc_formatter` (including Prettier conformance), `just lint -p oxc_formatter`, and the default-feature check completed. All three upstream failures disappear: formatter Babel positives improve from 2271/2280 to 2274/2280. Updated the coverage and fixture snapshots; output is stable on a second formatting pass.

AI disclosure: prepared and verified with Codex assistance.

prs.title: fix(react-compiler): keep the optional chain through a non-null assertion
prs.author: sarankumar1325
prs.body:
Fixes #28142

### Before / After

```tsx
users?.find((user) => user.id === userId)!.name
```

Before: `users.find((user) => user.id === userId).name` (the `?.` was dropped, so this throws when `users` is undefined)
After: `users?.find((user) => user.id === userId).name`

### Cause

In oxc the whole chain is one `ChainExpression`, and the lowering decides whether a member or call is optional by walking its receiver spine (`expr_contains_optional`). A `TSNonNullExpression` stopped that walk, and the `other` arm in the optional member/call lowering then lowered it as a plain expression. Babel keeps the chain going through `!`, so the inner link should still be an optional member/call.

### Fix

- `expr_contains_optional` looks through `TSNonNullExpression`.
- When the object of an optional member, or the callee of an optional call, is a `TSNonNullExpression`, it is lowered with `lower_chain_subexpr` so the inner link keeps its optional semantics.

### Tests

- New fixtures `optional-chain-non-null-assertion.tsx` (the issue repro) and `optional-chain-non-null-assertion-call.tsx` (`obj?.get!().value` and `obj?.get?.()!.value`), with snapshots.
- `cargo test -p oxc_react_compiler` passes with no changes to existing snapshots; `cargo clippy -p oxc_react_compiler --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` are clean.

AI disclosure: this change was written with help from an AI assistant and reviewed and tested by me.

prs.title: fix(react-compiler): preserve optional-chain cache guards
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
Memoization can hide a required `TypeError` after an optional chain short-circuits on an earlier render. For `obj?.a.b(getArg())`, rendering first with `obj = undefined` caches `undefined`; rendering again with `obj = {}` can reuse that result because the reduced dependency `obj?.a` is still `undefined`. The second render should throw when reading `.b`.

Keep non-optional continuation dependencies below optional prefixes instead of letting the prefix subsume them. When a computed or call continuation cannot be represented as a property path, retain the original optional guard dependency. For conditionally evaluated chains such as `getArg() ? obj?.a.b(getArg()) : null`, truncate an unhoistable dependency before its last optional link. This tracks the guard without moving a throwing read ahead of its condition. Fully optional chains keep their existing dependency reduction.

Adds 11 focused Node runtime cases comparing compiled and original JavaScript over two consecutive renders, with truthy and falsy conditions. They cover static, computed, optional-call, nested, conditional, and fully optional chains, plus method receivers. Output snapshots cover the generated dependencies.

This bug predates and is independent of https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/pull/28144. The same static, computed, and optional-call failures were reproduced with `babel-plugin-react-compiler@1.0.0` and `@babel/core@8.0.9`; this intentionally corrects behavior also present upstream.

prs.title: fix(react-compiler): keep manual memoization as written when its dependencies can't be honoured
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
The compiler could change when a manual `useMemo` or `useCallback` updates by replacing the author's dependency list with the dependencies it inferred. In the reported case, a list sorted with `useMemo(() => sortBy(items, s ?? props.value), [items])` started sorting again when `s` changed, even though the author had left `s` out of the dependency list. Extra dependencies could also be dropped.

Enable exhaustive memo dependency validation by default, matching current React Compiler upstream. When dependencies are missing or extra, skip the whole component or hook and leave its manual memoization intact. Other functions in the file can still compile. ESLint and Oxlint suppressions continue to work as before.

Regression tests cover missing and extra dependencies, partial `useCallback` dependencies, non-inline callbacks, property reads inside callbacks, and sibling compilation after a bailout. Validation passed: the full React compiler test suite, all 1,844 fixture snapshots, Clippy, and all 37 NAPI tests.

Fixes #27113

prs.title: fix(minifier): keep brackets on negative and non-finite numeric keys
prs.author: ozenyunus35
prs.body:
Fixes #27834

`try_compress_property_key` cleared `computed` for every numeric key, while the string branch only turns a key into a number when it is `>= 0`. A computed `-2` or `Infinity` key folded to a numeric literal then lost its brackets. Codegen puts them back for a non-method `ObjectProperty`, but not for methods, binding and assignment-target properties, or class members, so `{ [-1]() {} }` was printed as `{ -1() {} }`, which doesn't parse.

The numeric branch now only drops the brackets when the value is finite and has a positive sign, so `-2`, `-0`, `Infinity` and `NaN` keep them.

Added cases to `test_property_key` for each key position (object method, assignment target, binding, class field, static method, accessor) plus `Infinity`, `-Infinity`, `NaN` and `-0`; the method case fails without the change. `cargo test -p oxc_minifier` and clippy pass, and the five snippets from the issue now minify to code that runs and prints `7`, `7`, `1 3`, `5` and `7` in Node.

I used an AI assistant to help draft parts of the code and tests; I reviewed the changes and ran the tests myself.

prs.title: fix(react-compiler): emit valid binding names for hyphenated props in JSX outlining
prs.author: HawkForge
prs.body:
Fixes #26288

Thanks to @ADSA-DR for the report, and to @alfafc for narrowing it down and pointing to the upstream report (facebook/react#36218).

AI assistance (Claude) was used to prepare this change. It was verified with `cargo test -p oxc_react_compiler` and the new fixture snapshot.

Root cause: with `enableJsxOutlining`, `collect_props` used the JSX attribute name as the outlined component's prop name and as the binding name in its destructure. For names like `data-testid` or `aria-label` that is not a valid identifier, so the output contained `const { "data-testid": data-testid } = t0`, and `result.errors` was empty.

Change: derive a valid identifier from the attribute name (`data-testid` -> `dataTestid`, prefixed with `_` if the result is empty, starts with a digit or is a reserved word). The existing de-duplication then handles collisions. The original name is still used as the attribute on the JSX inside the outlined component, so the rendered DOM is unchanged.

Test: new fixture `jsx-outlining-hyphenated-attr.js` with its snapshot. Without the fix the snapshot shows the invalid destructure; with it the output parses.

prs.title: fix(semantic): separate hoisted vars from block type bindings
prs.author: limadog9
prs.body:
Fixes #22785.

When hoisting a `var`, the binder reused a same-name type alias or interface from an intermediate block scope. This lost the function-scoped value binding and left later value references unresolved. Only reuse intermediate bindings that can be referenced as values, so the block's type binding and the hoisted variable retain their own scopes and references.

The regression checks separate symbols and type/value references for aliases, interfaces, and nested blocks. The alias case fails before this change; TypeScript 6.0.3 accepts all three inputs.

Validation:

- `cargo test -p oxc_semantic --all-features`
- `CARGO_BUILD_WARNINGS=deny cargo lint -p oxc_semantic`
- `cargo test -p oxc_linter --all-features`
- `cargo test -p oxc_minifier --all-features`
- `cargo run -p oxc_transform_conformance` — committed conformance snapshots match.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

prs.title: feat(oxfmt): add debug span for reading files
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Reading a file happens outside the `oxfmt::format` span, so time spent in I/O did not show up with `OXC_LOG=debug`.

On a machine where an endpoint security agent scans every `open()`/`close()`, most of the wall time was spent there, but the log only showed formatting time.

```
DEBUG oxfmt::read{path=src/foo.tsx}: oxfmt::cli::service: close time.busy=92.6µs time.idle=2.38µs
```
